sections.title: As bright as the sun

q.prompt: Which word means “comparing two things using ‘like’ or ‘as’”?
q.reason: “simile” means comparing two things using ‘like’ or ‘as’.

options.fb: “sparkle” means shine with small flashes of light.

q.prompt: What is the garden like at night?

captions: Hello, and welcome to Camday English, Stage 4. In this lesson: As bright as the sun.
Recognise and use similes.
Here are some new words. Simile. Comparing two things using ‘like’ or ‘as’. Compare.
Say how two things are the same or different. Sparkle. Shine with small flashes of light.
Listen and say them. simile
compare
sparkle.
And some more words. Silent. With no sound at all. Gentle. Soft and kind, not rough.
Fierce. Angry, strong and frightening. Listen and say them. silent
gentle
fierce.
Time for a question. The video will stop.
Which word means: comparing two things using ‘like’ or ‘as’?
Now some grammar: Similes. A simile compares two things using ‘like’ or ‘as… as’.
For example: The snow was as white as sugar. For example: She ran like the wind.
Now listen, and read along. The night garden.
The garden at night is as silent as snow, The moon hangs above like a lamp on a pole.
The flowers are sleeping, their petals shut tight,
The fireflies sparkle like stars in the night.
A gentle breeze whispers as soft as a sigh, And an owl, like a shadow, glides quietly by.
Another question. The video will stop. What is the garden like at night?
Well done! Today you learned new words, like simile, compare, sparkle.
You practised similes. And you read The night garden. Now try the practice questions.
See you next time!

sections.title: Super sounds

q.prompt: Which word means “words close together that start with the same sound”?
q.reason: “alliteration” means words close together that start with the same sound.

options.fb: “slither” means move by sliding along the ground, like a snake.
“splash” means the sound of something hitting water.

captions: Hello, and welcome to Camday English, Stage 4. In this lesson: Super sounds.
Spot alliteration and put adjectives in a natural order.
Here are some new words. Alliteration. Words close together that start with the same sound.
Slither. Move by sliding along the ground, like a snake. Splash.
The sound of something hitting water. Listen and say them. alliteration
slither
splash.
And some more words. Tumble. Fall over and roll. Wriggle. Twist and turn your body.
Glisten. Shine because it is wet. Listen and say them. tumble
wriggle
glisten.
Time for a question. The video will stop.
Which word means: words close together that start with the same sound?
Now some grammar: Order of adjectives.
When we use two or more adjectives, opinion comes before size, then age, then colour.
For example: a lovely little red boat. For example: a big old grey cat.
Now listen, and read along. The snake, the seal and the squirrel.
A slippery, slithery, silvery snake Went sliding and slipping along by the lake.
A sleek, shiny seal gave a splash and a squeal, And swam in a circle to look for a meal.
A small, silly squirrel ran up a tall tree, Then tumbled and wriggled and giggled with glee.
Another question. The video will stop. Where did the snake slide?
Well done! Today you learned new words, like alliteration, slither, splash.
You practised order of adjectives. And you read The snake, the seal and the squirrel.
Now try the practice questions. See you next time!
